problem: Sending every weight position each federated round limits communication savings even after weights have been clustered.
contribution: FedCode usually exchanges only cluster centers in both directions, with periodic compressed-weight transfers to recalibrate client and server models.
reading_guide: Compare joint communication savings with accuracy loss; very large compression ratios can hide severe utility degradation.

diagram.title: Exchange codebooks, recalibrate periodically
diagram.description: The server sends its codebook, clients update and train local models, and their codebooks return to update the server model; calibration rounds also carry weight indices.

stages.title: Send global codebook
stages.detail: Cluster global weights and broadcast sorted centers to participating clients.

stages.title: Update and train
stages.detail: Map local weights to nearby received centers, then train on local data.

stages.title: Return client codebooks
stages.detail: Cluster each trained local model and upload its centers.

stages.title: Update global weights
stages.detail: Concatenate received codebooks, update global weights by nearest center, and start the next round.

diagram.footnote: Calibration is periodic in each direction: transmit codebooks plus weight indices; server-side calibration reconstructs models and applies FedAvg. The cycle returns to the first stage.

results.title: Bidirectional savings against clustering baselines
results.question: What does codebook transfer add beyond transmitting clustered weights every round?
results.context: CIFAR-100, ResNet-20, 10 clients, full participation, 100 rounds, 4 local epochs. FedCode uses 64 centers and calibration rates 0.2/0.5. Accuracy (%) and data transmission reduction (DTR, × FedAvg) are higher-is-better; no uncertainty reported.
results.interpretation: FedCode reaches 14.6× joint reduction with 58.07% accuracy. FedZip’s larger upstream reduction yields only 1.9× joint reduction because it does not compress the downstream route.
results.caveat: Dashes reproduce unreported entries in the source table, not zero communication. These results use one workload and the paper’s configured baselines; MUCSC was not reproduced.

results.title: Calibration controls the accuracy cost
results.question: How far can communication shrink before the model loses useful accuracy?
results.context: CIFAR-100, ResNet-20, 64 centers, 10 clients, full participation, 100 rounds, 4 local epochs. F1/F2 are the source table’s calibration-rate labels. Accuracy change is in percentage points versus FedAvg; data volume is reported in MB.
results.interpretation: The 264.7× ratio comes with a 46.88-point accuracy loss. The selected 0.2/0.5 setting reduces communication substantially while avoiding that extreme collapse.
results.caveat: No uncertainty is reported. The preprint inconsistently assigns F1/F2 to upstream and downstream in different sections, so the original labels are retained without relabeling their direction.

results.title: Partial participation under heterogeneous data
results.question: What accuracy cost remains when only 10% of clients participate each round?
results.context: 10 clients, 10% participation; IID Dir(10) versus non-IID Dir(0.1), with label and quantity skew. Accuracy changes are percentage points versus each FedAvg baseline; joint DTR is a multiplicative reduction. No uncertainty reported.
results.interpretation: Savings persist under partial participation, but the non-IID accuracy losses are larger than the IID losses in all four selected comparisons.
results.caveat: Appendix B uses longer runs for non-IID data and partial participation; MobileNet also uses more clusters for non-IID data. These rows are not controlled one-variable comparisons.

evaluation.label: Data and models
evaluation.value: CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet-20 and MobileNet v2; 12-class SpeechCommands v2 with YAMNet.

evaluation.label: Federated setting
evaluation.value: 10 clients; 10% or 100% participation; Dirichlet concentrations 10 and 0.1; Adam, four local epochs, batch size 128.

evaluation.label: Compared with
evaluation.value: FedAvg, FedAvg with weight clustering, and FedZip; MUCSC could not be reproduced from its reported clustering details.

evaluation.label: Measured scope
evaluation.value: Test accuracy, communication volume/DTR, and bits per parameter; computational complexity is analyzed, without a measured edge-device energy or latency benchmark.

limitations: This page uses the November 2023 arXiv v1 preprint, whose summary statistics differ from the IEEE EDGE 2024 published version. Results from those versions are not combined.
Codebook size, calibration frequency, participation, and training duration jointly affect the results. Savings from a selected setting are not a universal compression guarantee.
Reported tables contain no run-to-run uncertainty. Model- and distribution-specific settings differ, including up to 2,000 rounds in the MobileNet appendix.
FedCode is a communication method. Keeping raw data local and compressing updates do not provide a demonstrated privacy guarantee against inference or malicious clients.
takeaways: Avoiding repeated weight-position transmission can save more communication than clustering alone.
Periodic calibration is essential: relying exclusively on codebooks can greatly reduce accuracy.
Upstream-only savings can exaggerate practical benefit; inspect the joint upstream-plus-downstream metric.
